attempted_axis: Full 2026-08-31/09-01 law-wave screen of the v4 wall plus THREE probes on axes the v2/v3/v4 do-not-retry does not cover (it closed the update-form SPELLING axis at four identical A/Bs, nothing else). Probe 1, pointer-DERIVATION: moved `aPtr` from the pre-update base (`aPtr = v + 1` before `b = *(v += 2)`) to the post-update base (`aPtr = v - 1` after it), to force a second consumer of the ADVANCED pointer and so make the update-load the web's defining use - which is exactly the reopen condition v4 itself stated. Probes 2 and 3, the BLOCK-SCOPE CURSOR prescribed by claim.law.block-scope-cursor-restores-lwzu-where-mutation-sinks.20260831.v1, a law recorded 2026-08-31T15:47:20Z that post-dates the v3 park (04:28:29Z) by ~11h and was NOT in v4's screen: replaced the mutating `*(v += 2)` with a single-assignment cursor `f32* bPtr = v + 2; b = *bPtr; ... *bPtr = newB;` - first with the cursor declared before v's other uses (probe 2), then re-ordered so the cursor is v's LAST use (probe 3) to satisfy the law's explicit 'p must be dead afterwards' precondition that probe 2 violated.

attributes.decisive_finding: ALL THREE AXES ARE INERT, AND THE TWO NEW LAWS THAT LOOKED LIKE DIRECT HITS BOTH FAIL FOR NAMED REASONS. (1) The aPtr-DERIVATION axis produced a BYTE-IDENTICAL object to baseline (NEUTRAL, real 4, 43/43, multiset 2t unmoved): MWCC algebraically re-associates `v_new - 1` back to `v_old + 1` and re-emits the same pre-update `addi r5,r4,4` at 0x68, so the advanced pointer never acquires a second consumer. This closes v4's OWN stated reopen condition by measurement - the update-load cannot be made the web's defining use by re-deriving the second pointer, because the compiler folds the derivation back across the update. (2) The BLOCK-SCOPE CURSOR axis REGRESSED identically in both probes (real 4 -> 9, insns 43/42, multiset 2t -> 3t, same cluster `T[27:29]@6c-74=['lfsu','addi']` vs `O[27:28]@6c-70=['lfs']`), i.e. two identical A/Bs, which kills the axis. Fixing the law's stated precondition changed NOTHING: MWCC folds the single-assignment cursor into a plain displacement off the un-advanced base and drops the address computation entirely, so we LOSE an instruction (42 vs 43) and lose count parity. WHY THE CURSOR LAW DOES NOT TRANSFER, which is the reusable part: its verified case (select.c::serve_blits) walks a cursor along a LIVE, PERSISTENT record pointer where the advance must survive, so the addi is real and fuses with its load. WPitchMat3's loop RECOMPUTES the element base every iteration (`add r4,r31,r3` at 0x60 with `addi r3,r3,16`), the cursor has exactly two uses at one constant displacement, and nothing downstream needs the advanced value - so the cursor is a single-displacement alias and is folded away per claim.law.single-use-field-pointer-alias-is-folded-away. The law's precondition 'p is dead afterwards, as in a loop that recomputes the element pointer each iteration' is, for this function, the very thing that makes the fusion UNNECESSARY and therefore absent. The residual is fully localised to two words: 0x6c target `lfsu f4,8(r4)` vs ours `lfs f4,8(r4)`, and 0x84 target `stfs f0,0(r4)` vs ours `stfs f0,8(r4)` - one missing load-with-update fusion, whose absence forces the store to carry +8 instead of addressing the advanced base. 41 of 43 rows are byte-identical.
attributes.do_not_retry: All of v3/v4 stands: the update-form SPELLING axis is closed at four identical A/Bs, and the residual is an opcode substitution (lfs -> lfsu) plus a displacement change, so it is NOT webfrank-eligible under claim.law.webfrank-cannot-close-instruction-count-deltas and the permutation-guard family. ADDED BY THIS PASS, three further closed axes: (a) pointer-DERIVATION of the second store's address (pre- vs post-update) is byte-identical, because MWCC re-associates the offset back across the update; (b) the BLOCK-SCOPE CURSOR of claim.law.block-scope-cursor-restores-lwzu-where-mutation-sinks does not transfer to a per-iteration-recomputed base - measured twice, and it costs an instruction; (c) satisfying that law's 'base dead afterwards' precondition by reordering is inert. Do not re-probe any of these. NOTE for a future reopen: the source ALREADY contains the canonical update idiom `b = *(v += 2);` - the gap is not that the source fails to express the advance, it is that with the base recomputed each iteration MWCC has no reason to materialise it and folds every access to a displacement off the un-advanced base.
